The serpent star Ophiura albida reaches an ultimate disc diameter of 1.5 centimeters [Li = 1.5 centimeters], with arms extending up to six centimeters in length. This moderate body size positions the species among the mid-sized brittle stars of European continental shelf waters. At the onset of larval metamorphosis, individuals possess a disc diameter of just 0.02 centimeters , representing an approximately 75-fold linear increase from the metamorphic stage to the maximum adult dimension. The newly metamorphosed juveniles subsequently undergo a prolonged period of somatic growth before attaining sexual maturation. For populations maintained under controlled laboratory conditions at a stable water temperature of 10 °C [T = 10 °C], the interval from birth to the metamorphic transition has been documented at 17 days , a comparatively brief developmental period that aligns with observations reported for the congeneric Amphiura filiformis.

Reproductive maturity in Ophiura albida is reached when the central disc approximates 0.3 centimeters [Lp = 0.3 centimeters] in diameter, a size threshold that correlates closely with the initiation of gametogenesis and functional gonad development. The corresponding ash-free dry weight at this pubertal stage is estimated at approximately 0.0007 grams , a value derived from allometric scaling relationships that predict a rapid increase in tissue mass as disc diameter expands toward its ultimate limit. Under the thermal regime of 10 °C [T = 10 °C], the time since birth at which this pubertal milestone occurs has been recorded at 1.5 years [tp = 1.5 years], a figure closely matching the maturation schedule documented in the related species Ophiura ophiura. The extended pre-reproductive period suggests that resources are preferentially allocated to skeletal and somatic growth during the first eighteen months of benthic life.

The maximum reproductive output of Ophiura albida has been estimated through extrapolation from oocytic production and body-size constraints. Under optimal feeding conditions at 10 °C [T = 10 °C], a gravid female can produce approximately 250 eggs per spawning event [N_R_i = approximately 250 eggs per spawning event], a high per-event fecundity that reflects the energetic capacity conferred by the species' relatively spacious coelomic cavity and the sustained availability of high-quality phytoplanktonic prey throughout the prolonged spring phytoplankton bloom characteristic of the North Sea. This reproductive output, when combined with spawning events occurring at a frequency of approximately 1 spawning per day [F_R_i = approximately 1 spawning per day], yields a daily reproduction rate of 250 eggs per day [Ri = 250 eggs per day]. The continuous spawn output underscores an opportunistic reproductive strategy tuned to exploit brief but predictable peaks in pelagic primary productivity.

The ash-free dry weight of a fully grown adult Ophiura albida individual has been calculated at 0.0869 grams , an ultimate mass that is consistent with the species' disc diameter of 1.5 centimeters [Li = 1.5 centimeters] when the allometric scaling exponent of 2.694 is applied to the dry weight data. This asymptotic body mass is achieved only after several years of benthic growth and reflects the accumulation of both calcified skeletal plates and soft-tissue reserves in the arms and disc. The ash-free dry weight at puberty, approximately 0.0007 grams , represents roughly 0.8 percent of the ultimate adult mass. Such a low relative mass at maturity indicates that a considerable proportion of the species' total lifetime growth occurs during the post-pubertal phase, a pattern that is consistent with the extended lifespan typical of this brittle star.

The lifespan of Ophiura albida has been estimated to be approximately 15 years [am = approximately 15 years] when maintained at 10 °C [T = 10 °C], representing a relatively protracted existence for an ophiuroid of this disc size. The wet weight of a newly hatched larva at the moment of birth is approximately 0.0000005236 grams [Wwb = approximately 0.0000005236 grams], a value that reflects the small yolk reserves contained within an egg measuring roughly 0.1 millimeters in diameter. Following a brief incubation period of just 2 days [ab = 2 days] at 10 °C [T = 10 °C], the free-swimming ophiopluteus larva emerges and commences planktotrophic feeding. Metamorphosis to the benthic juvenile form requires a further 17 days  of larval development under the same thermal conditions at a temperature of 10 °C [T = 10 °C]. The attainment of sexual maturity, a milestone already described in the context of somatic growth earlier, is reached at 1.5 years after birth [tp = 1.5 years after birth] at 10 °C [T = 10 °C], marking the transition to reproductive competence.
